**A link to the Git revisions or merged pull requests with the implemented smart contracts and transactions for managing Hydra groups.**

Our team has implemented a HydraGroupRegistry validator and a HydraGroup minting policy to securely manage Hydra group records on-chain, along with the associated off-chain contracts for registering, disbanding, and discovering Hydra groups. Users can choose to participate in the evolution of the Cardano Racers ecosystem by forming independent Hydra groups and hosting Layer-2 races. By doing so, they can actively contribute to the decentralization and fairness of the platform while earning hosting fees as a reward. When a new Hydra race is announced, it will be linked to a specific Hydra group. This group will then be responsible for initializing a Hydra Head, processing the race, and publishing the results back to Layer-1 upon race conclusion.

All relevant smart contracts, transactions, and blockchain queries have been included in this PR:

https://github.com/mlabs-haskell/cardano-racers/pull/35

**A link to the Git location containing the bootstrapped Hydra application.**

We have bootstrapped a Hydra application using Hydra PureScript SDK. Hydra group participants will run this application to connect with Hydra peers and reach consensus on race simulation results when processing Layer-2 races. Currently, the application successfully executes the full Hydra workflow - from Head initialization to Fanout - though reward distribution remains hardcoded, as we plan to integrate the Unity consensus mechanism as part of the next milestone. Our planned approach to consensus handling involves each Hydra participant running a race simulation in detached mode with the same set of user inputs to verify that each user's result was achieved fairly. Once all results are processed and validated, rewards will be distributed to honest race participants, and hosting fees will be paid to Hydra group members.

ms.report:
Over the past month, we have made substantial progress in developing a functional Hydra-powered Cardano Racers prototype. While additional integration work is still required to connect all components and complete the milestone, the core Hydra workflow is largely implemented and operational.

The Unity application has been updated to execute in headless mode and accept user input via a CSV file passed as a CLI argument, enabling Hydra participants (or delegates) to run simulations as child processes.

We have added a new Hydra server endpoint that allows registered race participants to submit their inputs, enabling delegates to reproduce the run in Unity headless mode and reach consensus on the player's result. In that endpoint, several checks are performed to ensure all game conditions are satisfied. Specifically, we verify that the submitting user is a registered race participant, that participants cannot submit simulator inputs more than once to overwrite an existing result, that no concurrent simulations are currently running for the same user, and that the participant has signed the BLAKE2b-256 hash of their input and Race ID using their payment key. Once a valid submission is received, the input is forwarded to the race simulator, and the resulting time achieved by the player is then stored locally and becomes eligible for consensus processing. The simulator is spawned by the delegate and runs as a child process with a one-minute timeout. The timeout is needed to prevent malicious attempts to stall the Hydra operation by submitting deliberately malformed inputs that could cause the simulation to run indefinitely. The exact timeout value is yet to be determined and will be finalized as integration progresses and operational feedback is received.
